raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
ZenDNN reorders int8 MoE expert weights in place only when each expert has room for the `N * 4` byte compensation row that follows it. `process_weights_after_loading` leaves them packed back-to-back, so it falls back to duplicating every expert instead.

zentorch exposes the fix as an op, `zentorch_preprocess_weights` which re-allocates an `[E, N, K]` int8 weight with slack after each expert.
The op is merged on the zentorch plugin's main branch but is not in a released build yet, so on the pinned `2.14.0.1` this path is inert. `has_zentorch_op` returns `False` and the hook returns before touching a weight. It will reach the public package in an upcoming release.

## Validation

Unit coverage added to `tests/kernels/moe/test_zen_cpu_int8_moe.py`, which the `CPU-Kernel Tests` Buildkite job already collects:

```
$ pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_zen_cpu_int8_moe.py
11 passed
```

### What the padding buys

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B W8A8, 40 MoE layers, 256 experts, 32 cores per arm on one socket each. Both arms run the same install and differ only in whether the call added here is allowed to run

```
lm_eval --model vllm --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --limit 20 \
  --model_args pretrained=<Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8>,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096 \
  --batch_size auto --apply_chat_template
```

| | this PR | control (no slack) |
|---|---|---|
| layers padded | 40 | 0 |
| **peak RSS** | **70.9 GiB** | **90.7 GiB** |
| gsm8k exact_match  | 0.95 ± 0.05 | 0.95 ± 0.05

nodes.body:
## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

zentorch_preprocess_weights is not registered by the zentorch this repo pins (2.14.0.1: setup.py zen extra and ZENTORCH_VERSION in cpu.yaml). The wheel's libzentorch.so and _C.so have zentorch_fused_moe and zentorch_flush_moe_weight_cache but not this op, and public ZenDNN-pytorch-plugin main (0e95331) doesn't have it either. It does the same padding in Python in zentorch/vllm/_int8_moe_patch.py. So on a vllm[zen] install this gate returns for every layer, and CI only exercises the test's own mock. Could you name the zentorch version that ships the op (and the build behind the 71.3 GiB arm), and either bump the pin in this PR or note in the description that it is inert until then? Also, the body has the gsm8k command but the table has no scores. Could you add both arms, since the slack lets ZenDNN rewrite the weight buffer in place?

@@ -132,6 +135,67 @@ def _make_int8_moe_weights(use_bias: bool, dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16):
     return w13, w2, w13_scale, w2_scale, w13_bias, w2_bias
 
 
+@pytest.fixture
+def mock_zentorch_preprocess_weights():
+    """Reference zentorch_preprocess_weights, registered when zentorch is absent."""
+    if hasattr(torch.ops.zentorch, "zentorch_preprocess_weights"):
+        yield None
+        return
+
+    def _preprocess_weights(weight, zentorch_op_name=""):
+        if weight.dim() != 3 or weight.dtype is not torch.int8:
+            return weight
+        e, n, k = weight.shape
+        pad = ((n * 4 + 63) // 64) * 64 + 64
+        storage = weight.new_empty((e, 1, n * k + pad))
+        out = storage.as_strided((e, n, k), (n * k + pad, k, 1))
+        out.copy_(weight)
+        return out
+
+    lib_def = torch.library.Library("zentorch", "DEF")
+    lib_def.define(
+        "zentorch_preprocess_weights(Tensor weight, str "
+        "zentorch_op_name='zentorch::zentorch_preprocess_weights') -> Tensor"
+    )
+    lib_impl = torch.library.Library("zentorch", "IMPL", "CPU")
+    lib_impl.impl("zentorch_preprocess_weights", _preprocess_weights)
+
+    yield True
+
+    lib_impl._destroy()
+    lib_def._destroy()
+
+
+def test_zen_int8_moe_weights_get_per_expert_slack(
+    mock_zentorch_preprocess_weights, monkeypatch
+):
+    """Both projections reach the op, and only the Zen experts opt in."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(current_platform, "is_zen_cpu", lambda: True)
+    w13, w2, *_ = _make_int8_moe_weights(use_bias=False)
+
+    def _layer():
+        layer = torch.nn.Module()
+        for name, w in (("w13_weight", w13), ("w2_weight", w2)):
+            layer.register_parameter(
+                name, torch.nn.Parameter(w.clone(), requires_grad=False)
+            )
+        return layer
+
+    layer = _layer()
+    maybe_pad_zen_moe_weights(layer, ZenCPUExpertsInt8)

nodes.body: Could this live in ZenCPUExpertsInt8.process_weights_after_loading (today the base no-op) instead? This method already calls that hook at :253. Online int8 MoE (experts_int8 / int8_per_channel) calls it too at online/int8.py:131, and it selects ZenCPUExpertsInt8 with the same quant keys. That drops this identity check and the zentorch_utils import here, and online int8 on Zen gets the slack as well. ZenCPUExpertsInt8.init keeps only scales and biases, and apply reads the weights from the layer, so the later placement is safe. Fine as a follow-up.
